claims.text: The museum separates mobile settlement phases from the later Ulaanbaatar name. Wang’s abstract describes a specific Qing commercial office’s passport and monitoring remit, not all Mongol government. Kaplonski separately describes Sando’s expulsion and a new government in 1911. Name, site, office competence and regime change are different kinds of evidence; later diplomatic retrospectives cannot supply an uncollated original treaty or universal recognition.

claims.text: Does a mobile settlement’s name establish fixed-site foundation or uniform Qing governing power? A mobile-site chronology, a bounded passport office and a later regime removal establish distinct relations. Neither a name nor an amban-quarter site proves fixed 1639 location, all-Qing control or settled recognition.
